title: Cohorted Traffic Thermostat for Model Experiments
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight, cohort-aware A/B testing engine (the 'Traffic Thermostat') that allows PMs and platform engineers to define model-versus-model experiments with precise exposure controls, staged canaries, shadow traffic options, and automatic rollback when statistical or safety thresholds are breached. The feature should expose experiment setup in Console and API, integrate with existing observability (per-route dashboards and token-level cost), and support sequential statistical tests, alpha-spending, and minimum detectable effect (MDE) estimation. It must be usable for both hosted and Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Console: new experiment creation flow supports target cohort selection, exposure schedule, canary windows, and shadow routing
API: programmatic experiment creation/update/delete with JSON schema and idempotency
Exposure control: staged ramps (e.g., 0.5%, 1%, 5%, 20%), cohort pinning, and manual override
Statistical checks: sequential testing with configurable alpha spending, optional FDR control, and clear pass/fail signals
Auto-rollback: safe default policies that pause or revert traffic when safety metric breaches or p-value thresholds are exceeded
Metrics: integrates with existing evaluation hooks to collect latency, token cost, quality signals (ROUGE/embedding similarity/custom heuristics), and safety triggers
Shadow mode: ability to mirror traffic to a candidate model without affecting user-facing responses
Audit and logs: every experiment action (create/update/rollback) is recorded with actor and timestamp (works in Private/VPC mode with KMS-enabled audit logs)
SLO: experiment controller must operate within 100ms decision latency for routing and not add >2% tail latency to requests
design_notes: Prefer declarative experiment spec: exposures expressed as list of (time window, cohort, percent)
Cohorts should be definable by hashed keys (user_id, session_id, ip) with consistent hashing to ensure determinism
Statistical engine lives in control plane; sampling and metric collection use existing trace/metrics pipeline and will emit experiment-specific tags
Provide a "quiet" shadow mode to run full evals without affecting billing/metrics being reported to end users
UX: surface sample size estimates and expected time-to-significance before launching a ramp
engineering_notes: Spike: implement a minimal sequential t-test + AR(1) correction for temporal correlation (ENG spike assigned to Priya Patel)
Runtime routing: integrate thermostat with smart routing layer to ensure low-overhead deterministic routing decisions
KV cache implications: ensure mirrored/shadow requests do not pollute production KV caches unless explicitly opted-in
Data pipeline: EDH/metrics team must add experiment_id tag across generation, latency, safety verdicts
Backward compatibility: experiments default to 'fail-closed' (no traffic to candidate) if compatible model variant not found
rollout_plan: Week 1: Feature flag behind pm-experiments-v1; console + API scaffolding merged
Week 2: Sequential testing engine landed in control plane; basic exposure controls wired to runtime routing
Week 3: Internal dogfood: run 3 canaries (search, summarization, assist) in staging with smoke metrics
Week 4: Gradual beta with 5 customers on Dedicated; collect feedback and iterate
Post-beta: GA with Console onboarding flows and docs; support auto-rollback policy templates
test_plan: Unit tests for deterministic cohort hashing and routing decisions
E2E tests that validate exposure ramps and rollback triggers in a controlled traffic generator
Simulated A/B runs to validate type I error under sequential tests and alpha-spending parameters
Load tests to ensure controller scales to 10k experiments and does not add >2% overhead to request paths
Security review and penetration test for Private/KMS audit integration
